blocks.text: But that Bochart dealt no differently with Diodati than with Kimchi is asserted by the same Pococke, loc. cit.: "It is true," he says, "that the words of his that are cited are found in the Geneva quarto edition of 1607, namely that the grains were spoiled da soverchie piogge, by excessive rain; but in the later edition (Geneva 1641, in largest format) words are found which indicate exactly the opposite, namely that they could not sprout per lestreme ioccita, because of extreme drought, as if he remained in doubt with others whether this damage or that was brought on either by the frequency of rains or by their excessive scarcity, or, as some prefer, by joining both, after long-lasting rains, a raging drought, or the heat of the sun. But Kimchi, as has been said, does not attribute it to an abundance of rain, but to a lack or want of rain."

"But that ancient grammarian Abu Walid (under the words עבש and פרד) tries to draw out the meaning of the verb עבש by comparing it with the Arabic word عبس [ʿbs], inasmuch as it means the same as يبس [yabisa], to dry up, which he judges to fit this passage best, because the damage described here seems to have been caused by drought rather than by moisture, so that the words עבשו פרודות [III, 304] mean nothing other than אלתשניע ואלהעטים לאמר אלקחט אלדי נאלהם התי יבשת אלחבוב תחת אלארץ אד לא ינזל עליהא מטר פלם תנבת, to heighten the horror and the magnitude of the famine that overwhelmed them, so that the grains dried up under the earth, because rain did not fall on them, and so they could not come up. R. TANCHUM says that this too happened through a great drought, and he thinks it can be shown from this ان مع الجراد عدم الامطار [anna maʿa al-jarād ʿadam al-amṭār] that together with the locusts there was also a lack of rain there, which also appears from what follows (vs. 20.), כי יבשו אפקי מים, the channels of the waters have dried up." Thus Pococke, loc. cit. p. 81. 87 f.
That drought favours the increase of locusts is also shown with many examples by IGNATIUS DE ASSO, pp. 9, 15, German trans.
